AN253-R1.result: Original 4 modules x raw/Wire now match expectations; stale cases reject at old-address window check with/without consumer edge; valid controls accept.

findings.title: Handled CallClosure operations omit ordinary-argument symbolic F escape/signature checking
findings.location: crates/zil-analyze/src/forward.rs:611-675; fallback only at 677-689; owned_callbacks.rs concrete signature checking gated by owned_callbacks, excluding ordinary Copy-signature forwarded closures
findings.reproduction: F:Fn(i32)->i32 is taken to v0, then CallClosure(callee=v0, arguments=[v0]), then v0 is returned as Parameter(1). This passes raw and Wire Analyze even though ordinary argument expects i32 and receives symbolic F. Replacing the argument with a genuine i32 is the matched accepted control.
findings.expected: Reject F/Address<F> escape through ordinary callback parameters and check each actual callback argument/result against its declared signature independently of Verify.
findings.actual: Both invalid and valid modules accepted raw+Wire on exact 6c snapshot.
findings.minimal_fix: Audit argument operands for all handled CallClosure variants (local/shared/mut/value/once/borrowed); enforce actual argument/result types and reject symbolic callable provenance in ordinary callback argument slots. Prepay argument/type scans. Keep callee observation separate from ordinary arguments.
findings.scope_limit: Untrusted raw/Wire producer-kernel boundary, not a claim that source Types accepts f(f) or native execution is possible.
